title: Early players who made up tunes by ear, and the showboat
summary: Dejean could make up pieces for dances; country people had little music, and the French and Price showboat was where they heard bands and bought music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, that band I had, the first band I had, the old boys could do that. I mean, anything they hear, they could just go ahead and play. In fact, when we first started, everybody could just, well, Dejon, the man I told you that knew so much music and couldn't explain it, one would play a dance that way, he could just make up a piece and everybody would dance and play it and give it any name. And at that time, we didn't have people that knew anything about music. Anybody that would hear a piece of music, they wouldn't know what it is. They didn't have a grab a phone, they didn't have anything like that. They knew music. You could tell them anything and it was that. In fact, they didn't know how to dance hardly. Especially the white people, they didn't know how to dance at all. And I'm surprised to see how the people that danced now. And music, very few could play music. I mean in the country, you know? I don't remember the city and big places. Well, the only time we would hear music here on the show board would pass. That would be twice in the wintertime, you'd get a show board pass. What show board was that? French and Price. That's the only time we'd see a movie picture. We didn't have nothing like that in the country.

French and, yeah, they would even have a show board pass on the river. You know, they'd stop at the reserve and go across the river. And until they get to New Orleans, they go back. What band would they have on the show? They have a good band. They had a good band. We used to buy music from them.
Do you remember the guys in the band? The name of them?
No, no, no. I don't remember. I don't even know the name. We used to buy music. You know, go around and sometimes they give us a few pieces.
What about Dajon's tunes? Did any of them become popular later? His children? His tunes that he would make up like that.

Well, we never had kept, why don't we keep it up, you know? It would have been alright if we would have brought it, you know? Just play that way until, in fact, most of the pieces that we play... Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
